verifiedJob.name: AOT scheduler, HTTP ranges and font fallback

method.statistics: Arithmetic median (mean of two ordered values for n=2), observed min and max; no confidence intervals or significance claims.
method.timingPopulation: Only run-1-control and run-4-control. Instrumented diagnostic times are kept separately and are not product performance.
method.counterPopulation: Instrumented runs 2 and 3; external HTTP/font/correctness counts checked across all four runs.
limits: One GitHub-hosted Linux x64 machine; only two control process launches per configuration.
Conditions run in a fixed order inside each process. Per-task and per-document samples are correlated, not independent process replications.
First native-PDF pass follows the no-op scheduler burst sequence and is not a fresh OS-cache or fresh-engine cold start.
Process CPU includes the harness, native worker, and loopback HTTP server where applicable; 10 ms ticks cannot isolate short scheduler CPU costs.
Queue ages and selection/execute wall times are instrumented observations, not UI latency or unmodified product times.
Measurements of first 384 px raster do not establish first visible sharp frame, responsiveness, viewport quality or GPU cost.

findings: No-op bursts demonstrate excess canceledOnly queue scanning: at 4096 tasks the instrumented worker made 4,939,415–5,298,792 canceled probes for 4,097 selections (one selection is a measurement command).
Actual mixed PDF workloads peaked at queue depth 39–40, much below the artificial 2,752–2,936 burst peak. 32 extracted pages and eight raster submissions completed per workload.

Every workload returned four uncancelled images totaling 761,856 pixels; all four immediately cancelled raster requests returned no image. This does not count internal cancelled render work or prove zero native work.

Control mixed-workload times are about 363–396 ms. Instrumented UXLC queue-age maxima are 192–202 ms; GCC maxima are 48–52 ms. These are separate instrumented diagnostic observations, not product/UI latencies.

The scan implementation is an upstream worker concern. These data justify bounding submitted background work and exploring the upstream queue, but do not establish an app performance gain from a queue rewrite.
limits: Returned pixels are output-buffer pixels, not total native rendered/abandoned pixels.
No scheduler-only unmodified CPU measurement was collected.
The instrumentation adds one worker metrics command per row.
Cancellation is immediate after submission, not mid-frame interaction.

E10.firstRasterDefinition: Elapsed backend time from pdfDocumentFromUri start through a completed 384px-wide first-page raster; no Flutter frame/viewport. useProgressiveLoading is left at false.
findings: At 64KiB ranges the original GCC document needed 51 requests and 3,304,571 bytes; the linearized file needed 54 requests and 3,477,090 bytes (98.15% of its file), in both initial and repeat opens.

At 1MiB ranges both files needed four requests. On the zero-delay loopback condition the control initial first-raster medians were 480.832 ms (original) and 509.436 ms (linearized), versus 530.3395 and 608.571 ms with 64KiB ranges. The sample is too small for a general recommendation.

With 15ms delay per request and 8MiB/s server pacing, 64KiB-range control initial first-raster medians were 1496.733 ms (original) and 1538.7385 ms (linearized). A server responding HTTP200 once yielded 737.700 and 772.1785 ms, respectively. This compares server response modes, not an app patch.

Repeat opens downloaded the same bytes and request counts. The fixture advertises public,max-age=3600 and a fixed ETag, but never returns304. This establishes behavior only against this server; it does not measure successful304 cache reuse.

Twenty concurrent reads of one missing block produced twenty serialized requests (1,310,720 bytes), not one. Read bytes were correct. This is direct evidence of missing same-block single-flight in the tested reader.
Eight retained URLs added eight 65,687-byte cache files; dispose did not evict them in this finite workload. Authentication identities had distinct cache paths. No global long-term quota was tested.
limits: Real internet transport, TLS, HTTP304, failures/retries and progressive-loading=true were not exercised.
The original and linearized files contain the same pages but differ in byte size.
The input PDF is already resident in the local server process.
Overlap/quota subcases capture the real cache reader through a stub document entry and do not execute native PDFium.

sourceExplanation.interpretation: The locked code skips revalidation only when mustRevalidate&&isFresh. Our fixture has max-age but no must-revalidate; its non304 response invalidates existing cached blocks. This source reading explains the observed repeat downloads without claiming a measured fix.

findings: With ten distinct missing face names, each run and both eager/progressive modes reported nine foreign fixture faces on document0; only one of ten documents reported its own expected face within the observation window.
The shared-face case also reported its common name for one of ten documents, but cannot identify cross-document affinity because every document requests the same name.

Ten explicit concurrent identical PdfFontManager requests performed ten resolver calls and ten payload loads when cold. Instrumentation recorded ten registrations and ten reloads. Repeating with the registered face kept ten resolver calls but performed zero payload loads, registrations and reloads.

The control manager-loading interval was 15.279–15.831ms cold (median15.555ms) and0.034–0.037ms registered (median0.0355ms). These are cache-state observations of the same manager, not a measured app optimization.
All ten explicit-manager document results in every run extracted the expected Hebrew word and produced identical nonempty raster hashes (155 ink pixels).
limits: Missing-font fixtures are synthetic and deliberately unembedded; automatic application fallback was disabled for event-attribution cases.
Only events delivered during the harness window are counted. Some native render missing-font notifications are asynchronous; this does not prove that other documents never receive later events.
The explicit-manager subcase is separate from automatic application fallback/event routing.
A Hebrew string and nonempty identical pixel hashes do not prove glyph appearance, layout fidelity or absence of tofu.
The common face name cannot expose foreign-face affinity by construction.

applicationCandidate.action: Coalesce concurrent identical font loads/registrations and share the immutable bundled Tinos payload, while preserving per-query fallback/style behavior and retry after failure.
applicationCandidate.reason: Cold duplicate resolver/payload/registration/reload work is directly counted; current application fallback uses a shared manager but does not itself coalesce identical pending calls.
applicationCandidate.requiredProof: Measure PdfFontFallback itself under concurrent PDF opens with text/pixel parity, event-loss/retry behavior, and no regression for distinct faces or styles.

practicalDisposition.supportedNow: Duplicate cold payload/registration work is measured.
practicalDisposition.notEstablished: Product UI speedup or safe universal event-serialization policy.

practicalDisposition.supportedNow: Distinct fixture faces are attributed to document0 in both modes.
practicalDisposition.applicationAction: Keep existing real-font fallback; avoid broad semantic changes without a product reproduction/parity test.

practicalDisposition.supportedNow: Large artificial bursts require millions of cancellation probes; actual mixed PDF depth is about40.
practicalDisposition.applicationAction: Retain bounded/coalesced background submission and existing cancellation; no queue rewrite speedup claimed.

practicalDisposition.ownership: upstream engine; no measured application HTTP-open change
practicalDisposition.supportedNow: Duplicate block transfers, repeated downloads against this non304 server, and finite retained-cache growth are observed.
practicalDisposition.applicationAction: Do not change app download block sizes or impose destructive eviction from these two local runs alone.
